newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds heavy, braced for rough ride.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds heavy, braced for rough ride.

text.p: *Australian bonds looked fairly heavy at the close as the market braced for another rough ride in after-hours trading against the backdrop of twitchy U.S. Treasuries.
Australian bonds looked fairly heavy at the close as traders braced for another rough ride in after hours trading against the back drop of twitchy U.S. Treasury market.

The June 10-year bond futures contract see-sawed around key support at 91.950 for most of the session, where a decisive break is expected to trigger off sell stops and exaggerate any further downward move.
"We've been pretty soggy all day. We're still bullish on the market but I think we have to get March 25 out the way first," said one trader.
The Federal Open Market Committee meeting gathers on March 25 and there is much debate as to whether it will endorse a tightening in U.S. interest rates.
"I think a 25 basis point hike is factored in and the market could take this as a responsible move. Anything more, and I think it's a completely different call," the trader added.
The markets have been on red alert for a possible rate rise since last month when Fed chairman Alan Greenspan warned of a pre-emptive tightening.
The U.S. faces February housing starts later today and before Wednesday's key U.S. CPI report for the same month.
A dearth of local data has left the direction of domestic bonds pretty much in the hands of developments in the U.S.
A 5.9 percent in fourth quarter Australian housing starts was in line with expectations and had no impact on the market.
"These figures only confirm that the housing recovery began before the end of 1996, which everybody knows by now anyway," said Chris Caton, chief economist at BT Australia.

However, traders reported a positive response to New South Wales Treasury Corp's tender of a new line of 2008 stock, and was able to allot A$360 million of bonds rather than the A$300 million originally offered.

The local market underperformed, although the whole dollar bloc remains under a cloud from the woes of the U.S. The Australian/U.S. 10-year spread is seen meandering in a 110 to 130 basis point range up until the FOMC meeting.
